followupNotes: Existing dirty work backed up to /tmp/emulsion-resume-backup/existing.patch and untracked.tar before edits. No commits, pushes, or changes to the original photo/sidecar.

Historical Texture collapse coincides with focus loss. A synthetic mid-drag blur reproduces its pass signature: heldRef clears while the harness continues inputs, repeatedly rebuilding Clarity and Sharpening. Focused baseline 56.7 fps / 10 ms GPU; final focused Texture 57 fps / 11 ms GPU at 63.7%. Remaining gap failures are real.

Gesture reports now include validity and timestamped blur/visibility interruptions; the CLI rejects invalid samples. Settle timeouts fail instead of silently returning incomplete results. VITE_PERF_BLUR_AT=10 deliberately exercises the interrupted lifecycle.

Develop tracks pointer release independently of engine.inexact, stages the final input even if prior live maps were exact, and defers a quiet held gesture until release. The regression was red before the fix and now covers pointer-up, blur and pointer cancellation with a final finished screen frame.

Real-photo output visually reviewed at 50%, 63.7% and 75% against the full-density renderer, plus 100% output and Sharpening-only pairs. Fine bridge stone, paint/metal edges and foliage lose texture. The lower-density settled policy is not accepted as a fidelity-equivalent replacement. Neutral reference remains within 1/255; 1:1 effects remain within 1/255.
The first per-effect comparison was discarded because source editing triggered HMR during the run. Only the uninterrupted densityeffects-final run is recorded as resumePhotoFidelity.

A first zoom-stop anchor assertion used fractional synthetic cursor coordinates and accumulated about one device pixel of WebKit rounding. The driver now uses a fixed integer cursor and asserts at most half a device pixel. The actual zoom implementation and performance thresholds were not changed.

All timings are individual samples from the real visible WKWebView, run serially. Chrome is used only for correctness. New small-pan coverage does not certify a large pan that leaves the cached region.
